bibliographic.title: Right to be forgotten in the Era of large language models: implications, challenges, and solutions
bibliographic.authors: Dawen Zhang; Pamela Finckenberg-Broman; Thong Hoang; Shidong Pan; Zhenchang Xing; Mark Staples; Xiwei Xu
bibliographic.citation_apa: Zhang, D., Finckenberg-Broman, P., Hoang, T., Pan, S., Xing, Z., Staples, M., & Xu, X. (2024). Right to be forgotten in the Era of large language models: implications, challenges, and solutions. AI and Ethics, 5, 2445–2454. https://doi.org/10.1007/s43681-024-00573-9

methodology.sector: AI technology and data protection law
methodology.technology_context: Large Language Models, chatbots, LLM-enabled software systems, GPT-3, PaLM, differential privacy, machine unlearning, model editing, guardrails, privacy-preserving machine learning

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article directly addresses LLMs and chatbots under GDPR/RTBF compliance and proposes technical governance mechanisms including guardrails, but its primary focus is privacy erasure rights rather than conversational governance architecture, human oversight, observability, or operational accountability of conversational systems.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only front matter and partial body text were provided; full-text sections on challenges, guardrails implementation, and limitations may alter eligibility weighting for conversational governance.

appraisal.notes: Conceptual legal-technical paper with structured sections on legal principles, LLM data practices, challenges, and solution categories. No empirical sample or explicit systematic review protocol is evident in the provided text.

cerqual.explanation: The argument coherently links GDPR/RTBF obligations to LLM-specific data practices and mitigation options, but the provided excerpts do not establish systematic evidence synthesis or empirical validation; relevance to conversational governance is partial and mainly through privacy/compliance and guardrails.

coding.theme: Privacy and data-rights governance for LLM systems
coding.subtheme: Right to be forgotten implementation challenges and technical mitigations

synthesis.main_claim: LLMs used in chatbots are not excluded from the Right to be Forgotten, and their non-indexing storage and processing create new GDPR compliance challenges that may be addressed through differential privacy, machine unlearning, model editing, and guardrails.
synthesis.contribution: Maps RTBF legal principles to LLM/chatbot contexts, explains how generative models differ from search-engine indexing, and organizes technical solution space into privacy-preserving machine learning and post-training methods.
synthesis.limitations: Provided text states solution approaches require further research and that the paper does not aim to provide an exhaustive list of advances; broader methodological limitations of the study design are unclear from the excerpt.
synthesis.use_in_review: Include as supporting evidence on privacy/compliance governance for regulated LLM and chatbot systems, especially RTBF obligations, data-subject rights, and technical guardrails/unlearning controls.
